w: French colonial administrators raised this as the plain 'Church of Saigon' between 1877 and 1880; it only became Notre-Dame in 1959, the year a statue of Our Lady of Peace was installed out front. Its twin brick bell towers, unrendered since construction, still rise 58 metres over downtown Saigon.
s: Colonial cathedral, renamed Notre-Dame only in 1959
_facts: Cathedral built 1877-1880, originally named the Church of Saigon
Renamed Notre-Dame Cathedral in 1959 when a statue of Our Lady of Peace was installed
Two bell towers reaching 58 metres (190 feet)

w: French-built and still doing the same job it always has - the city's government still runs out of this ornate pile facing Nguyen Hue Boulevard, through the colonial era, the war years, and everything since. Now a National Heritage Site, it opens its doors to the public just one weekend a month.
s: French-built city hall, still doing the same job
_facts: Houses the Ho Chi Minh City People's Council and People's Committee, facing Nguyen Hue Boulevard
Used as an administrative building through the French colonial period and the Vietnam War
Now a Vietnamese National Heritage Site, open to the public the last weekend of each month

w: Construction began in 1974 and did not finish until 1994 - two decades bridging a war - leaving this 32-metre Christ figure on Mount Nho as one of the largest Christian statues in Asia. A staircase of 133 steps winds up inside the hollow body to the outstretched arms, which span more than 18 metres over the coastline.
s: A 20-year build for one of Asia's tallest Christ statues
_facts: 32-metre statue of Christ the King on Mount Nho, built by the Vietnamese Catholic Church starting 1974, completed 1994
133-step staircase inside the statue; arms span 18.3 metres, total monument height 36 metres
Largest Christian statue in Asia since 2012, restored in 1993, major pilgrimage site

w: Commissioned by a French admiral in 1864 and opened to the public five years later, this is one of the oldest zoos on earth still on its original site. The grounds also hold the city's History Museum, plus a temple to the Hung Kings that started life as a WWI monument to fallen Indochinese soldiers.
s: One of the world's oldest zoos, since 1864
_facts: Commissioned by Admiral Pierre-Paul de La Grandiere in 1864, opened to the public in 1869
One of the world's oldest continuously operating zoos; botanical gardens founded by Jean Baptiste Louis Pierre
Grounds include the Ho Chi Minh City Museum of History (25,000 artefacts) and the Temple of Hung King, formerly a WWI Indochinese soldiers' monument

w: An octagonal fortress the French built in the early 1940s to replace the old Saigon Grand Prison - and every government since has kept using it. The eight-sided layout of cellblocks, walls and watchtowers was meant to make escape nearly impossible; in its whole history, only two attempts have actually succeeded.
s: An octagonal colonial prison, escaped twice ever
_facts: Octagonal prison on a 7-hectare site, built by the French Indochina government around 1939-1943 to replace the Saigon Grand Prison
One of 12 national prisons in Vietnam, used by all succeeding governments
Considered one of the highest-security prisons in Vietnam; only two successful escapes in its history

n: Mariamman Temple, Ho Chi Minh City
w: Raised in the late 1800s by Chettiar merchants from Tamil Nadu who had settled in colonial Saigon to trade, this temple to the goddess Mariamman is one of the last visible traces of the city's small historic Indian community. It's still tended today by descendants the founding priest helped raise.
s: A Tamil merchant temple from colonial Saigon
_facts: Hindu temple dedicated to the goddess Mariamman, built in the late 19th century
Built by the Nagarathar, a Tamil Nadu trade community
Now managed by the local Vietnamese Indian community connected to priest Attangudi Lakshmanan Chettiar

w: Three names for three eras: Rue Catinat under the French, Tu Do ('Freedom') Street under the Republic, and Dong Khoi ('uprising') since reunification - the same stretch of pavement running from Paris Commune Square down to the Saigon River, renamed each time the city changed hands.
s: Same street, three names across three eras
_facts: Street formerly known as Rue Catinat, then Tu Do Street, now Dong Khoi Street
Runs from Nguyen Du Street, opposite Paris Commune Square, to the Saigon River waterfront
